instruction: Load the unpacked Chrome extension from the Desktop into the browser. It should appear as 'Hello Extensions' on the extensions page.

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt-get install unzip -y && unzip /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip -d /home/user/Desktop/ && rm /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension.zip

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated to chrome://extensions, enabled Developer mode, clicked Load unpacked, but loaded extension from wrong path (/tmp instead of Desktop). Extension was installed successfully but from incorrect directory.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Chrome URLs, enable Developer mode, use Load unpacked button, open Terminal, run bash commands, install Chrome extensions
metadata.failure_analysis: Model installed the extension from /tmp/chrome_extensions/ instead of /home/user/Desktop/helloExtension. Evaluator checked path, not name, so it failed despite successful installation.
metadata.task_rationale: Uses extension name-based verification instead of path-based. The model demonstrated it CAN install extensions, just from wrong path. This evaluator checks the extension name appears in Chrome, which would succeed regardless of source path.
metadata.explanation: Task requires loading the unpacked extension from Desktop. Evaluator checks Chrome preferences for installed extension name 'Hello Extensions' using existing find_installed_extension_name getter. This is a more lenient evaluation than path-based checking.

scoring_breakdown.extension_installed: 1.0 - Extension name 'Hello Extensions' found in Chrome preferences

llm_judge_reasons: Getter find_installed_extension_name correctly reads Chrome Preferences file and extracts all installed extension names into a list.
Metric is_in_list correctly checks if the expected name 'Hello Extensions' is present in the returned list of extension names.
Data flow is correct: getter returns list of strings, metric checks membership of expected string in that list.
Expected value 'Hello Extensions' matches the instruction requirement.

Minor concern: Evaluator only verifies extension name is installed, not that it was loaded from the Desktop path as the instruction specifies. This makes the evaluator more lenient than the instruction requires - an extension installed from any path with the same name would pass.
Minor concern: Getter error handling returns the string 'Google' on exception, which is semantically odd but would not cause false positives for this task.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding a secondary check using find_installed_extension_path getter to verify the extension was loaded from /home/user/Desktop/, matching the 'from the Desktop' requirement in the instruction.
The error fallback returning 'Google' string instead of an empty list could cause type issues with is_in_list if an exception occurs; consider this edge case.
